__comment: 70s hi-fi separate: brushed aluminium faceplate with two VU meters, flanked by wood end caps that ReceiverBlockEntityRenderer draws in the chosen finish, like a speaker casing. The needles are NOT in the texture - they are drawn by ReceiverBlockEntityRenderer, which shares the meter constants. Faceplate art is 224x96px sampled at uv [0,0,14,6] onto a 14x6 face, which is 16px per block unit in BOTH axes, so unlike the speaker fronts there is no aspect pre-distortion here. See tools/generate_receiver_textures.py. Four output tubes rise through cut-outs in the heatsink top, drawn with their sockets and cages by the renderer; their glow is thermal, not signal-following - see core/TubeThermalModel. The glass envelopes are NOT in this file: they are drawn by ReceiverBlockEntityRenderer on a render type that does not write depth, because glass that writes depth occludes its own filament.

elements.__comment: Chassis. North is the faceplate; every other face is brushed casing, with uv chosen to match each face's proportions so the grain keeps an even texel density. It stops at z=12.5 and has no top face: AmplifierChassisRenderer draws the heatsink top with its tube cut-outs, the fins and the rear terminals.
Tube 1 anode stack, suspended inside the glass. Solid, opaque, and sized so there is clear glass all around it - that gap is what makes it read as being INSIDE something.
